notes: Seventh sweep (2026-10-31): five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at head 0814e8d with uncommitted: false; every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, reads empty and skills_listed 209. The prompt's last line is "Do not invoke any skills." Four runs wrote blog.ex in a single Write call with no other tool call; opus-1 wrote it, parsed it with Code.string_to_quoted!/1, wrote it again and parsed it again (three Bash calls, no skill read).

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix, as in 2026-10-23: the six ecto-phoenix.md rules, plus Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call and Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order. git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes one of the eight, the multi-line argument rule, graded against its current text below. The six ecto-phoenix.md rules and the directive-order rule are unchanged and graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/ecto-phoenix-baseline.json and its skill twin.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, current text: the sentence that decides every verdict is "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name, a short literal, or a trailing keyword list: a map or struct that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, that rule). A multi-line from/2 passed straight into Repo.all/1 is a call argument that is none of the three, so the 2026-10-23 reading still holds (opus-1 lines 84-89, sonnet-2 lines 95-101); a from(...) piped into Repo.all() still goes to Write pipelines (sonnet-1 lines 80-86); a multi-line literal that is a fn's return value is still not counted (haiku-1 lines 81-86). Inline multi-line maps in Log.changeset(%Log{}, %{...}) are violations in haiku-2 (123-128), sonnet-1 (124-129) and sonnet-2 (137-141). The trailing-keyword-list sentence only confirms render(conn, :show, post: post) and repo.update_all(query, set: [...]) as clean; the more-than-six-elements sentence is not triggered, since no literal in any run has more than four elements. opus-1's repo().query!("""...""", [last_id, next_id]) at lines 196-203 passes a heredoc string, which the rule's map-or-struct clause does not name, and is not counted. 4 of 5 violated (5 of 5 in 2026-10-23): haiku-1 is clean because its only multi-line struct is the Multi.insert fn's return value.

Keep migrations to schema changes: 5 of 5 violated, as in every baseline sweep. haiku-1 (line 108), haiku-2 (line 12), sonnet-1 (line 14) and sonnet-2 (line 21) run an UPDATE in the column migration. opus-1 keeps the column migration to the column (lines 157-161) and moves the backfill into a second, batched migration, BackfillPostsPublishedAt (line 165), using raw SQL on the posts table, not the schema; graded violated on "Put data changes in a separate script, Mix task, or release task", as the 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 baseline opus-1 runs with the same shape were. No run uses MyApp.Blog.Post in a migration.

Validate input with changesets: haiku-1 (lines 25-29) and haiku-2 (lines 39-43) omit a user constraint for their belongs_to, decided by "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`) so a violation returns `{:error, changeset}` instead of raising." opus-1 (foreign_key_constraint(:user_id)), sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (assoc_constraint(:user)) are clean. Every run casts only [:title, :body] and sets user_id on the struct. haiku-1's %Log{} of code-set values is not the params-built struct the rule names (the sweep-b reading). Same tier pattern as 2026-10-23.

Group writes: all five use Ecto.Multi with Repo.transaction() and normalize Multi's four-tuple to {:error, reason} (opus-1 moved from Repo.transact/2 in 2026-10-23). opus-1 and sonnet-1 guard a double publish with a conditional update_all in Multi.run returning {:error, :already_published}; sonnet-2 locks the row FOR UPDATE in Multi.run. Load associations: every listing preloads (opus-1 by preload: [:user], haiku-1 and haiku-2 by |> preload(:user), sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 by join plus preload). 404: every controller calls a context function over Repo.get!/2 (opus-1's get_visible_post!/2 pipes a visibility query into Repo.get!/2). Every controller calls only the context. Directive order: 5 of 5 clean.

Changed rules outside the list, checked as other_violations: no run has with, cond, if, a capture or an Enum call. Every case clause in the five runs is a short table row (ok/error or match/no-match), so the rewritten `->` rule is not broken. One new finding: sonnet-2 lines 133-135 put a one-expression fn body on the line below its head where the one-line form fits in 92 characters, which the new sentence "A `fn` body is laid out like any other body: one expression stays on the head's line" in Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer forbids. No do: body holds a fn, and no one-line pipeline has two steps; the single-step DateTime.utc_now() |> DateTime.truncate(:second) in haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and sonnet-1's from(...) |> Repo.all() are recorded under Write pipelines as before. haiku-1 and haiku-2 leave MyApp.Blog without @moduledoc. Comments that state assumptions, requirements or reasons are not counted, as in 2026-10-23.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As in previous sweeps, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, add, remove, alter, from, execute, embed_templates and the rest) in locals_without_parens: all five pass. The only line over 98 characters is a comment, sonnet-2 line 4 (100 characters), which the formatter does not wrap. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.

Error reasons: no run returns a string reason or Multi's four-tuple. opus-1 and sonnet-1 return {:error, :already_published}; sonnet-2 returns {:error, :not_found} and {:error, :already_published}; haiku-1 and haiku-2 pass the failing changeset through.
